corroboratedFacts: Equipment can supply the black Fire Attack conversion.
Yang checks actual Hand entities shown publicly during this phase across all participants. A deck/Processing reveal followed by obtaining is not a Hand-show instruction.
Cards already in the original user hand create no extra gain. Cards outside Hand at settlement cannot be obtained.
Self Fire Attack can trigger Shilu and then obtain the newly Shilu-shown foreign Hand card with that same Yang.

implementationDecisions: Miuyan delegates declaration, black material eligibility, payment, normal target legality, Nullification, actual Fire Attack reveal/same-suit discard and all damage children to the native single-card ordinary-trick conversion. Real Hand, Equipment and WoodenOxGrain materials retain exact physical provenance. Other conversions and pure played responses do not issue Miuyan.

A scalar invoice belongs to the native CardUseFrame, freezing accepted actor/provider, original skill instance/hash, actual turn, actual round, actual phase, physical cost and polarity. The existing conversion state toggles once on the real accepted Use declaration, independent of later damage. Actor replacement does not create a new entitlement.

Both Yang benefit and Yin failure are decided after the entire genuine native Fire Attack Use completes. The positive whole-Use damage ledger is authoritative; FireAttackResolved.CausedDamage is emitted before actual damage and is not proof. This whole-Use timing follows rule wording and the native return order, and ensures the complete self-damage Shilu subtree precedes Yang. No official specialized first-damage/whole-Use FAQ was found.

Phase Hand-show history is event-derived even while no player currently owns Miuyan. Explicit native public reveal producers are classified at emission, and only exact entities currently in Hand qualify. Private inspection, Processing/deck reveals, exact Shandao top-placement movement exposure and exact Zhaosong face-up gift movement exposure are excluded. Public Hand comparison, actual public hand drafts and Qingliang use their original native entities or original public binding. Classic Kangkai and Fanjian retain their explicit current content instruction to show the actual Hand card; the contributor guide example does not override a different implemented product/variant text. The older native Juanxia Fire Attack public Hand display is recovered from its exact scalar trick event while the owning native program still retains the original Fire-stage target/entity; it qualifies regardless of whether the optional same-color damage payment was made.

A qualifying phase-history entity may change holder, leave Hand and return, and still qualify if it is physically in some living character Hand when Yang freezes its gain set. This deliberately differs from Shilu continuous Hand identity. These transfer/reentry details follow the current wording and guide Hand-at-check rule; they are recorded as implementation inferences rather than official specialized FAQ. Own Hand entities create no synthetic movement or gain.

Yang freezes current foreign Hand entities once and moves exactly those entities in a native multi-source gain batch. Native gain/HP/skill/dying children return through the owning ProgramSkillFrame without replacing cards or repaying a completed gain. The issued native Use survives subsequent source loss; a dead owner performs no new gain.

An undamaging Yin issues a scalar suppression for the original owner and skill for the current actual round, independent of runtime instance. Qualification remains blocked after loss and regrant, and releases at a genuine next RoundStarted boundary. Shilu is unaffected.

Shilu observes PerDamage, not PerDamagePoint. At instruction execution it freezes max(0,current HP), performs that actual native draw and drains its native gain children before selecting a currently in-range living other participant with Hand cards. All private Hand choices use opaque frozen slots; only the chosen original entity is publicly revealed.

Shilu actual entity name is Slash through the canonical Hand identity query, including native card uses and response producers. Its original issuer/source/hash and real public reveal are retained in scalar facts after skill loss or issuer death. The identity lasts one continuous target Hand residency and ends on the first true departure; same Hand reordering is not a departure and later return does not revive it. This lifetime is an explicit rule/client-structure inference because the public client does not expose the server target-list removal rule.

All pending resolution state belongs to its actual native Use or ProgramSkillFrame. Exposed receipt collections clone on construction and init, new events carry only scalars or immutable scalar records, and private choices are projected through CreateSnapshot(viewerSeat). No use-ID sidecar, forged Use, fake phase or hand injection is used.
